Subject: Private deployment pricing/questions for pilot

Hi Chloe —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. HealthSpan is keen to move a pilot of your private (VPC) offering into a small production environment, but procurement needs clarity on two commercial levers before we can engage legal: the platform fee vs node/device credit model, and how SRE/managed hours are priced and billed. A few specific questions: 

- Can you provide an explicit comparison: 1) modest annual platform fee + lower per-node credit vs 2) $0 platform fee + higher per-node charge with a minimum commit? We need sample math for a 6–12 month pilot (approx 10 GPU nodes peak).
- Do you offer a migration/implementation rebate or one-time credit tied to onboarding milestones? If so, how is it applied (invoice credit, service credit, or rebate)?
- For SRE/managed hours: do you sell blocks (e.g., 50 hrs/month) or time-and-materials? Are 24/7 oncall options available for production?
- Can you confirm SOC 2 / evidence we can insert into our evaluation packet (we sent an RFP PDF attached).

Can you send a short term-sheet we can share internally (procurement + infra) covering these options? We prefer clear anchor pricing so procurement can compare to competitive bids.

Best,
Emma

Hi Emma —

Really appreciate the clear list — I attached a short pricing sketch to make the numbers concrete (pilot-pricing-draft.xlsx). High-level answers below, and looping in Marissa (commercials) + Irene (legal/product) to confirm details / any SOC2 evidence you need.

Quick answers: 
- We typically offer two lead commercial approaches for pilots:
  A) Platform fee (annualized) + lower per-node credits — good for predictable throughput and when customers want to avoid per-node variability.
  B) Zero platform fee + higher per-node credits with a minimum commit — lowers upfront cash but increases unit cost.

- Migration/implementation rebate: we can offer a one-time migration credit tied to onboarding milestones for pilot-to-production conversion. Typical size is negotiated (we've done 10–25% of first-year platform fee historically).

- SRE/managed hours: we sell monthly blocks (eg. 50 hrs / 100 hrs) or T&M for ad-hoc. 24/7 oncall available as an add-on (higher rate). For pilots we usually propose a smaller retained block + option to burst.

Next steps: Marissa — can you draft two concrete term options (numbers so procurement can compare)? Irene — can you share SOC2 summary + evidence pack link? Emma — I'll aim to get a clean term-sheet to you by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Chloe

Chloe / Irene —

Per Chloe's ask, I ran two clean commercial options to present to HealthSpan procurement. Numbers are illustrative for a 12-month pilot that peaks at ~10 GPU nodes (we assume general-purpose A100-equivalent pricing for node credits).

Option 1 (Platform-anchored) — recommended for predictable unit economics:
- Annual platform fee: $60,000 (covers control plane, telemetry, observability, basic support tier)
- Node credits: $0.06 per GPU-hour (billed monthly against usage)
- Migration credit: 20% of first-year platform fee ($12,000) credited across first 3 invoices upon completion of milestones (onboarding sign-off, successful data sync, 30-day runbook handover)
- SRE add-on: 50 hrs/month at $250/hr (retainer) — includes business-hours oncall and 2 scheduled escalations per month. 24/7 oncall available at $325/hr
- Minimum commitment: none for pilot; production conversion triggers annualization of platform fee and consumption smoothing adjustments.

Option 2 (Consumption-first) — for customers avoiding upfront platform fees:
- Platform fee: $0 (pilot)
- Node credits: $0.095 per GPU-hour
- Migration credit: limited to implementation assistance (one-time professional services credit up to $8,000)
- SRE: T&M; standard T&M rate $300/hr (no included retainer). 24/7 oncall available at $400/hr
- Minimum commit: 6-month consumption estimate required (for budgeting)

Rationale: Option 1 lowers per-hour unit economics and gives procurement an amortizable platform cost we can credit back on conversion. Option 2 is cash-light but more expensive per-token/node.

Approval asks: 
- Chloe: do you want to anchor HealthSpan on Option 1 or present both?
- Irene: confirm legal constraints on the migration credit wording and whether the credit should appear as an invoice credit vs SOW concession.

If we present Option 1, I can produce a one-page term-sheet + DocuSign link.

—Marissa

Chloe —

Thanks — we reviewed both options internally. A few counterpoints from procurement/finance: 

- Platform fee: HealthSpan prefers a lower anchor for pilot. Can you do $45k (instead of $60k) for the pilot, with the migration credit increased to 30% of first-year platform fee if we convert to production within 12 months?
- SRE: we need 24/7 oncall for production. For the pilot, we'd like 24/7 included for the initial 30 days post-go-live, then move to a retained block. Can you reduce the SRE hourly to $220/hr for the retained block?
- Migration credit mechanics: procurement prefers an invoice credit applied to month 2–4 invoices rather than SOW-level concessions.

I've attached our redlines for quick reference. If we can get close to the two changes above we can fast-track to legal.

Thanks,
Emma

Marissa / Irene —

HealthSpan pushed back with clear asks: lower platform fee to $45k (pilot) and increase migration credit to 30% on conversion, want invoice credit mechanics, and request 24/7 included for the first 30 days. They also want SRE retained rate at $220/hr.

My recommended compromise to close quickly:
- Platform fee: agree to $48,000 for the pilot (split invoicing quarterly)
- Migration credit: 25% of first-year platform fee ($12,000) applied as invoice credits across months 2–4 after go-live (milestone gated)
- SRE: offer 30 days 24/7 coverage post-go-live as part of onboarding; retained block 50 hrs/mo at $220/hr thereafter (option to upgrade to 24/7 at $300/hr)
- Legal: allow migration credit to be an invoice credit (makes finance happy) — Irene, can you confirm we can word this without increasing indemnity or exposure?
- Commercial: Marissa, can you approve a $12k discount (effectively the 25% rebate) as within the deal desk flexibility?

If we can agree internally I will send a cleaned term-sheet and updated DocuSign today. HealthSpan indicated speed to legal if we move on these points.

Thanks,
